answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-personhood at each decision vertex: before an agent can spend treasury funds, it must present a fresh cipher-based attestation signed under a hardware key whose public root lives in a tamper-resistant ferrous-shielded secure element. Cloning that key costs real silicon per identity, so spinning up a thousand fake agents no longer scales — each sybil node needs its own chip, making mass attacks economically pointless.
